question: My offer says 90k. What actually hits my account every two weeks?

figures.label: Wages subject to federal and Colorado income tax
Wages subject to Social Security, Medicare and FAMLI
figures.note: The 401(k) lowers income tax but not FICA; the Section 125 medical premium lowers both.

figures.label: Federal income tax withholding
figures.note: Pub 15-T 2026 Worksheet 1A: annualize, subtract $8,600 (line 1g, single, Step 2 unchecked), Single STANDARD row $57,900-$113,200: $5,800 + 22% over $57,900.

figures.label: Colorado income tax withholding
figures.note: DR 1098 2026: no DR 0004, so $5,500 allowance for single; 4.40% flat.

figures.label: Denver occupational privilege tax
figures.note: $5.75 per month, taken from one check a month. This case is the first check of a month (the Jan 22, 2027 pay date on the sample stub).

figures.label: Net pay (first check of the month)
figures.derivation: gross_pay - pretax_401k - medical_premium - federal_withholding - social_security - medicare - colorado_withholding - colorado_famli - denver_opt

figures.label: Net pay (a check with no Denver OPT)

must_include: Gross pay per check is $90,000 / 26 = about $3,461.54, using the biweekly frequency from the offer letter.
Each deduction is shown on its own line: 401(k), medical premium, federal withholding, Social Security, Medicare, Colorado income tax, Colorado FAMLI, and Denver OPT.
Net pay of about $2,417 per check (about $2,423 on checks without the $5.75 Denver OPT).
Says the 401(k) and medical premium are pre-tax: the 401(k) lowers income tax but still pays Social Security and Medicare.
Says these are estimates of withholding, not the final tax bill, and that the W-4 choices change the federal line.
Links salary and pay frequency to offer_letter.pdf page 1.
must_not_include: Taxing the full $3,461.54 for federal or Colorado income tax (ignoring pre-tax deductions).
Using the pay stub's illustrative tax lines ($312.40 federal, $136.00 Colorado) as the answer.

assumptions: Profile 'default': single, Denver, employee-only PPO 750, 6% traditional 401(k), no dental or vision, matching samples/pay_stub.pdf.
2020+ Form W-4: single, Step 2 unchecked, Steps 3 and 4 blank. No Colorado DR 0004.
Medical premium is a Section 125 deduction: exempt from income tax, Social Security, Medicare and FAMLI.
Uses 2026 tables because 2027 Pub 15-T and DR 1098 are not out yet; the sample start date is Jan 4, 2027. Re-derive when they publish.
Rounding: each line rounded to cents; net is the sum of rounded lines.

sources.what: Federal withholding: Pub 15-T Worksheet 1A, line 1g $8,600, Single STANDARD schedule
Social Security 6.2% to the $184,500 wage base; Medicare 1.45%
Colorado FAMLI 0.88% of wages, up to half (0.44%) from the employee

notes: The pay stub's tax lines are illustrative (see samples/answers/pay_stub.json); its gross, 401(k) and medical lines match this case. FAMLI drops to 0.86% (0.43% employee) in 2027 per an Oct 2026 announcement; update with the 2027 tables.
